records.board_basis: Apollo 204 Review Board, account of the ground test and Board findings on test conditions and emergency egress.
records.board_locator: Ground-test account and Board Finding 4 (emergency egress)
records.claim: The plugs-out ground test exposed the crew to hazards inside the command module even though the Saturn IB was not fueled.
records.evidence_boundary: It does not show the cabin atmosphere, electrical condition, hatch status or test decisions.
records.image_description: Apollo 1 crew Gus Grissom, Ed White II and Roger Chaffee standing outside near Launch Complex 34 during training.
records.image_evidence_limit: A training photograph cannot prove cabin atmosphere, test approval decisions or the point of ignition; those findings come from the Apollo 204 Review Board.

records.board_basis: Apollo 204 Review Board, Part VI, Board Findings, Determinations and Recommendations, Finding 2.
records.board_locator: Part VI, Finding 2 (100-percent oxygen atmosphere and pressure)
records.claim: The Board recorded a 16.7 psia, 100-percent oxygen atmosphere during the test and classified the conditions as extremely hazardous.
records.evidence_boundary: Oxygen supported the rapid fire; neither oxygen nor this photograph identifies the ignition source.
records.image_description: Command/Service Module 012 being moved for mating to the Saturn Lunar Module Adapter at Kennedy Space Center.
records.image_evidence_limit: The preparation photograph cannot depict oxygen concentration or pressure. Do not treat it as a sensor trace.

records.board_basis: Apollo 204 Review Board, reconstruction of events from 23:20 GMT through the first fire report, and voice transmission analysis.
records.board_locator: Part V, Data Analysis, S-Band Transmissions; Part IV, fire-report sequence
records.claim: The first crew transmission reporting the emergency began at approximately 23:31:04.7 GMT.
records.evidence_boundary: The report does not prove ignition started at 23:31:04.7; the training photograph is not telemetry or footage of the fire.
records.image_description: The Apollo 1 crew preparing to enter Command Module 012 in an altitude chamber during training.
records.image_evidence_limit: Do not recast a 1966 crew-training image as 1967 fire telemetry. A reported event is not necessarily its initiating event.

records.board_basis: Apollo 204 Review Board, cabin-pressure reconstruction and emergency hatch chronology.
records.board_locator: Part V, Data Analysis, Cabin Pressure Rise; Part VI, Findings 3–4
records.claim: The pressure vessel ruptured at about 23:31:19 GMT, at an estimated pressure of at least 29 psia; emergency egress could not be completed before rupture.
records.evidence_boundary: The museum-era photograph does not depict a 1967 rupture, a pressure trace or the accident hatch being operated during the test.
records.image_description: Apollo 1 tribute spacecraft mockup and hatch display photographed at Kennedy Space Center in 2017.
records.image_evidence_limit: The photograph provides later exhibition context. The rupture timing and pressure are investigative findings, not values inferred from an image.

records.board_basis: Apollo 204 Review Board, Part VI, Finding 1 and associated fire-origin analysis.
records.claim: The Board judged an electrical arc the most probable initiating source but identified no single conclusive ignition point.
records.evidence_boundary: Damage is evidence of the fire and its effects, not a photograph of the original arc, its location or its exact start time.
records.image_description: Interior of Command Module 012 after the Apollo 1 fire, showing intense heat damage.
records.image_evidence_limit: Visible heat damage is not a photograph of the initiating arc. The exact wire, location and instant of ignition remain unproven.

records.board_basis: Apollo 204 Review Board safety recommendations and subsequent NASA redesign history; the Board report itself is not evidence that all later redesigns were completed in 1967.
records.board_locator: Part VI, recommendations; subsequent NASA response for completed modifications
records.claim: The response included an outward-opening hatch and broader changes to materials, wiring, testing and safety practices.
records.evidence_boundary: A 2017 exhibit documents a later display; it is not a photograph from the accident or proof that the hatch was the only corrective action.
records.image_description: Redesigned outward-opening Apollo hatch exhibited at the Apollo 1 tribute at Kennedy Space Center.
records.image_evidence_limit: The 2017 display is not an image of the 1967 accident itself. The changes cannot be reduced to the hatch alone.
